section_map.summary: The summary routes a coach-evaluation task through AHP, Grey Correlation, Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation, time adjustment, sensitivity, and a final three-sport Honor Roll.
The introduction establishes the demand for an all-time coach comparison, states three requested lists, bounds gender claims, and previews the model ladder.
The paper fixes comparability assumptions, defines coach and sport indicators, and introduces the symbols that later receive AHP weights.
The overview reduces fifty-four candidate factors to a three-level hierarchy, explains the retained criteria, and assigns the parallel ranking models.
The AHP section creates hierarchy levels, pairwise matrices, consistency checks, criterion weights, and seven retained indicators.
Grey Correlation normalizes coach indicators, computes relation coefficients and degrees, and turns the weighted values into sport-specific rankings.
Fuzzy evaluation defines comment grades, membership matrices, weight vectors, and a combined score for the same coach comparison.
The results review compares Grey and Fuzzy rankings, names the leading coaches, and frames agreement as a practical ranking cross-check.
The time adjustment adds a coaching-start-time index to address changing competitive opportunities and produces adjusted score lists.
The sensitivity section perturbs the largest AHP weight, reports rank movement, and bounds the claim as local ranking stability.
The discussion returns to the three requested coach-comparison problems, summarizes the completed model route, and states the scope of the resulting lists.
The Honor Roll turns the ranked outputs into three named sport lists and makes the requested communication artifact immediately scannable.
The strengths, weaknesses, and conclusion return from the parallel models and adjusted scores to a bounded claim about evaluating outstanding coaches.
The Sports Illustrated letter translates the ranked evidence into an audience-facing explanation with an explicit selection rationale.
The references show a mixed provenance base of websites, rankings, and method sources while leaving several data and calculation details unresolved.
The appendix presents additional tables, MATLAB-oriented calculation material, and ranking support without supplying a complete executable reproduction package.

assumptions.summary: The selected indicators can compare coaching achievement within each stated sport despite changing eras and competition conditions.
Fifty-four candidate factors can be reduced to a three-level hierarchy and seven retained measurable criteria.
The gender coding and associated effect used in the source are appropriate for the stated comparison, although the rationale is not demonstrated.
A coaching-start-time index with a seven-percent weight represents the intended historical opportunity adjustment.
Changing only the maximum AHP weight by plus or minus 0.02 is informative about the stated local rank sensitivity.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The Summary identifies the requested comparison of outstanding coaches and the final three-sport Honor Roll.
The model overview reports fifty-four candidate factors, three top-level dimensions, and a final seven-criterion selection.
AHP tables give pairwise judgments and weights for achievement, winning, longevity, honors, player development, gender, and related factors.
Grey Correlation uses coach records and normalized indicator values to produce sport-specific relation degrees.
Fuzzy evaluation introduces comment grades, membership values, and a grade vector for the same coach comparison.
The results tables show Grey and Fuzzy ranks for selected basketball, baseball, and football coaches.
The adjusted ranking adds coaching-start year through the stated time-index convention and seven-percent weight.
Sensitivity tables report changes after the maximum criterion weight is perturbed by 0.02.
The conclusion says data came from NCAA, while earlier pages cite Wikipedia and sports websites; both provenance claims are retained.
Appendix tables contain supporting coach records and a Harry Statham win total that conflicts with a body-table value.

Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation produces a parallel rank list using grades and membership aggregation.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The Summary gives a complete task-to-model-to-list route before technical detail.
The paired rank table visibly connects two computations to a selection decision, but award status alone does not show why judges valued it.
The letter turns a transparent method route into an audience-facing artifact, without proving a causal judge preference.

weaknesses.summary: The two-factor AHP matrix reports lambda=2.0000 together with CR=0.2496; those values are inconsistent under the stated consistency formula.
Prose calls some three- and four-factor comparison matrices two-factor matrices, leaving the hierarchy description internally inconsistent.
The male=1 and female=3 coding uses an unsupported gender rationale and should not be transferred as an evidence-backed comparison rule.
Grey normalization prose confuses min and max cases and changes the evaluated entity from coaches to countries.
The Fuzzy table duplicates d13 and omits d14, so the grade or membership index cannot be safely reused without source reconciliation.
The final fuzzy expression uses Z=B D^T although D is defined as five elements and B earlier denotes top-level weights, creating a dimensional and semantic conflict.
The paper says Fuzzy evaluation both considers and does not consider internal relationships, so the claimed distinction is unresolved.
The time index (T-1900)/100 and seven-percent weight are weakly sourced and systematically favor later-starting coaches under the stated convention.
Changing only the maximum weight by plus or minus 0.02 supports conditional rank sensitivity, not indicator validation, parameter robustness, model validation, or external validity.
Comparison with Wikipedia or current ranks risks circular validation and candidate-selection bias when the same ecosystem supplies the inputs or benchmark.
The conclusion attributes data to NCAA while the body cites Wikipedia and sports websites, leaving the actual data provenance unreconciled.
Appendix reports Harry Statham wins as 1076 while an earlier matrix reports 1079.
MATLAB or computer simulation is claimed without code, configuration, input data, or reproducible outputs.

independent_extensions.summary: Recompute every pairwise matrix from archived judgments and reconcile lambda, CI, and CR before using AHP weights.
Publish criterion data, normalization directions, and an auditable Grey calculation notebook.
Define fuzzy grade sets and membership functions, reconcile symbols, and test dimensions before score aggregation.
Use independent historical or expert-held-out benchmarks rather than rankings sourced from the same web ecosystem.
Justify, estimate, or scenario-test time adjustment separately from base achievement indicators.
Vary coherent weight vectors and indicator definitions, then report rank uncertainty rather than one maximum-weight perturbation.
Archive code, package versions, input tables, outputs, and a cross-table consistency test.
